Dispatch & Operations video

See how customer load intake becomes an operating record.

The customer load intake video belongs in Dispatch & Operations because the intake record starts the work BOF checks: customer request, lane, proof requirements, documents, assignment, safety, settlement, and billing follow-through.

Open customer load intake

Start readiness gates

Dispatch release depends on more than the BOL image.

BOF keeps load packet readiness separate from equipment readiness, driver readiness, and route/HOS readiness so the release decision explains the actual consequence.

GateRelease evidenceDispatch consequence
Load packet readinessBOL, rate confirmation, appointment detail, dispatch release noteRelease stays in review until the commercial and load packet records match the lane.
Equipment readinessPre-trip equipment photo set, last DVIR review, open defect clearance, trailer suitabilityRelease held until tire, light, coupling, trailer ID, and visible defect checks clear.
Cargo readinessCargo condition photo, seal photo, securement photo, BOL matchRelease remains in review until cargo condition, securement, seal, and BOL match are confirmed.
Route/HOS readinessAvailable hours, ETA risk, weather, parking, restrictionsLoad moves to watch if appointment timing cannot be met within available HOS.

Example Proof Packet · Blocked

Sample release blocker panel showing why dispatch should not commit the move just because a load exists in the TMS.

Controlling blocker
Credential hold, missing BOL, rejected proof image, or unresolved equipment defect
Cargo / seal proof
Required photo or seal requirement not yet attached to the packet
Owner
Named dispatcher, safety lead, or packet owner must resolve the blocker
Decision
Blocked until the controlling evidence clears

Dispatch operating checklist

Every release decision shows what clears the load and what blocks the move.

BOF turns customer load intake into a reviewable operating record: load packet, driver assignment, equipment readiness, route/lane review, traffic or weather exception review, and pre-trip release status stay together before dispatch commits the lane.

Pre-Trip Release

Dispatcher confirms driver eligibility, equipment readiness, cargo proof requirements, appointment detail, and release owner before the move is treated as ready.

Ready / Watch / Hold

Route / Lane Review

Lane notes can include route restriction, appointment risk, available hours, weather watch, traffic delay, parking, and customer timing review.

Exception review

Equipment Readiness

Truck, trailer, DVIR notes, visible defects, trailer ID, load suitability, and photo proof can stay connected to the release decision.

Equipment gate

Driver Assignment

Driver profile, DQF status, medical card, credential holds, safety notes, and dispatch consequence travel with the assigned load.

Driver gate

Release decisions

Dispatch sees allowed, warning, review, and blocked in plain language.

BOF keeps the dispatch answer visible in one pass: what can move, what must wait, which record is missing, and who owns the next step.

Allowed

Driver file, carrier packet, insurance, and trip packet are complete enough for dispatch to release with confidence.

Release

Warning

Load can move, but a renewal, document item, or owner note needs attention before it becomes a blocker.

Watch

Review

Dispatcher, safety lead, or document owner must confirm the record before release. TMS-LD-10482 lives here until BOL evidence clears.

Manager check

Blocked

Missing credential, packet hold, or safety item prevents assignment and gives the owner a named action.

Do not move

Governance basis

Dispatch proof is supported by document-handling controls.

BOL image review, mobile capture, and release records are treated as controlled operating evidence before dispatch trusts the lane.

Data classified

BOL images and release packets are handled according to classification expectations.

DAT-IT-004

ELD/mobile controlled

Driver uploads and mobile records are supported by device and ELD security controls.

DAT-IT-006

Review trail required

Release decisions name the reviewer, owner, record, and dispatch consequence.

Release note

Security governed

Security and access expectations sit behind the operating records without cluttering the dispatch board.

Lifecycle 01

Load enters board

TMS-LD-10482 appears with driver, carrier, lane, pickup time, owner, and document requirements already attached.

Lifecycle 02

Records are checked

Driver readiness, carrier packet, load packet readiness, equipment readiness, cargo readiness, route/HOS risk, and insurance are compared before dispatch commits.

Lifecycle 03

Owner action is named

S. Turner owns the BOL confirmation, so the dispatcher knows who clears the final step.

Lifecycle 04

Release with confidence

Once the packet is approved, the load moves from review to allowed with a visible record trail.

Who uses this

Dispatchers and operations leads deciding whether TMS-LD-10482 should move, wait, or go back to a document owner.

What it shows

Each release decision is tied to driver, carrier, document, lane, owner, and record status.

Operational consequence

A missing document item changes the load from release-ready to review, watch, or hold before the problem reaches the road.

What happens next

The named owner fixes the blocker, confirms the record, or releases the load with confidence.

Dispatch photo context

Dispatch decisions need the record trail beside the load trail.

BOF keeps route status, driver readiness, desk tools, and pre-trip paperwork in the same operating conversation.

Exception report review

Owners see what is blocked, why, and who owns the next action.

Field proof check

Dispatch consequences stay tied to evidence from the field.

Record clerk desk

Daily follow-up depends on clear status and reachable records.

Yard operations check

Route decisions are stronger when yard context is not separated.
